claim: For kappa=0, |lambda|<=B, beta=tau L^2, and every finite nonnegative nearest-neighbor coefficient a_L>=0 (including sequences tending to infinity), the full finite-chain Gibbs state is uniformly trace-close to the free XX Gibbs state, hence converges to the same continuum Fock density operator. The hard-rod endpoint is included as the a_L=infinity limit.
proof: proof.txt Section 9: sector min-max z^0_{L,m}>=z^a_{L,m}>=z^hc_{L,m}; exact squeeze x_j->x_j-(j-1) maps the hard-rod sector to free fermions on L-m sites; dominated convergence gives identical fixed-m endpoint heat traces; free Chernoff tail controls m; D(rho_a||rho_0)<=Z_0-Z_a and Pinsker give whole-state convergence.
inputs: Public J,tau,B and sign a_L>=0; unknown a_L is not acquired. This theorem is isotropic and uses exact number conservation.
cost: Explicit parameter-blind archive: p_bad<=C_E/[4 tau J(M+1)^2]+C_Z S_r; choose each term <=epsilon^2/18. Then q=ceil(log2(1+sum_{j<=min(M,r)} binom(M,j)))=O(log^2(1/epsilon)/loglog(1/epsilon)); mode transform O(N^2) gates plus reversible ranking, workspace and output charged separately. If physically synthesizing a_L=eta L, worst-case p>=ceil(log2(16 tau L^4/epsilon)) bits for eta.

Exact repulsive scattering nevertheless has node length ell=a_L/[4J cos(K/2)+a_L] in [0,1], and its hard-rod shift vanishes after division by L. Thus the Born term does not imply a nonzero repulsive continuum Gibbs interaction.

claim: For g in a compact interval [g_-,g_+] with g_->0 in a_L=-4J+g/L, the fixed-particle two-body limit is a repulsive Lieb-Liniger problem, but a uniform-in-L all-particle-number heat-trace/tail bound and whole-Fock Gibbs trace theorem have not been proved here.
proof: Two-body phase and Robin boundary are derived in proof.txt Section 10. The m-sector critical operator is exactly a killed SSEP configuration-graph Laplacian plus (g/L)W, and W>= (2m-L)_+ gives z_{L,m}<=binom(L-1,m)exp[-tau g_- L(2m-L)_+]. For any fixed integer k0 with 2 tau g_- k0>tau B+log(2), the total grand weight of m>=L/2+k0 is <=L exp[-(2 tau g_- k0-tau B-log(2))L]. This still leaves m<=L/2 and a fixed-width band uncontrolled. Existing primary sources give continuum/thermodynamic limits but not the needed finite-volume all-m estimate.
inputs: Open chain, compact positive g window, compact lambda interval, beta=tau L^2.
cost: No claimed archive bound for this attractive-near-critical microscopic coupling; missing step is a uniform grand-partition bound on a slightly enlarged detuning interval or an equivalent summable canonical-sector estimate, such as z_{L,m}<=A^m exp(-c m^2), plus a uniform high-mode estimate for whole-Fock convergence.
baseline: Repulsive Lieb-Liniger thermodynamics and the exact open XX free/repulsive family.
falsifier: Either a proven uniform sector heat-trace estimate or a macroscopic-number counterexample in the stated positive-g window.
novelty: UNKNOWN; do not extrapolate fixed-m convergence or thermodynamic Bethe ansatz to trace-norm convergence.
